title: Session Bridge Adapter — personal design scrapbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick capture of ideas for a lightweight Session Bridge Adapter (SBA). Goal: allow multiple short-lived client sessions (mobile/web) to be multiplexed into a smaller number of server-side LM sessions without losing per-client semantics (conversation, permissions, billing). This is a personal scratchpad — lots of TODOs and half-baked edges.

Constraints and goals:
- minimize tokens / KV-cache duplication across clients with similar prefixes
- preserve low tail latency for interactive clients (50–200ms in P95 for short turns)
- allow client disconnect/reconnect, offline resume, and handoff to other devices
- per-client isolation for privacy and billing (no leaking mutable state)
- compatible with Redwood runtime's KV caching and prefix sharing heuristics

High-level idea:
- SBA maintains one or more long-lived server sessions (S-session) per tenant/region/policy bucket.
- Each client session (C-session) is represented by a thin session projection: a small metadata descriptor + incremental delta log.
- S-session keeps a master KV cache and a set of ephemeral per-client overlays that are applied at request time.

API surface (rough shapes):
1) Create client session (client -> SBA):
POST /v1/sba/sessions
body: {"client_id":"string", "tenant":"tid-123", "initial_prompt":"...", "policy_flags": ["no-telemetry"]} 
response: {"c_session_id":"c-xxx", "attach_point":"s-yyy", "ttl_seconds":3600} 

2) Attach + call (Web socket or HTTP streaming):
WS /v1/sba/sessions/{c_session_id}/attach
- on open: auth + fetch small resume token
- messages: {"type":"input","seq":1,"text":"...","metadata":{}}
- server returns streamed chunks with bridge-level events: {"type":"bridge_event","kind":"prefetch_hit"}

3) Snapshot / flush client deltas to durable store:
PUT /v1/sba/sessions/{c_session_id}/snapshot -> returns snapshot_id
Used when client goes idle or for periodic checkpointing. Snapshots are small: sequence pointer, small set of context anchors, compressed delta.

4) Transfer/handoff:
POST /v1/sba/sessions/{c_session_id}/handoff -> {"target_device":"device-id"} 
Server ensures the next attach with a valid token gets the latest snapshot.

Config knobs (per-tenant):
- s_session_mode: ["shared", "dedicated", "tenant_shard"]
- max_c_per_s: integer (typical 32–1024)
- overlay_strategy: ["rebase-on-request","inline-merge"]
- idle_checkpoint_secs: 120
- prewarm_on_attach: boolean (if true, the S-session warms KV cache for expected prefix)

Session overlay model (conceptual):
- overlay = small ordered list of operations: [append_prompt, redact, anchor(label, offset), resume_token]
- when a C-session request arrives, SBA constructs an execution prefix: prefix = base_prompt + chosen_overlay_views
- base_prompt and KV cache are long-lived and shared; overlays are per-C-session and kept ephemeral unless snapshotted.

Event flow (ASCII):
Client A connect -> SBA finds s-1 (shared) -> apply overlay A -> request forwarded to runtime -> runtime uses KV-cache s-1 -> response -> SBA extracts per-client deltas -> stream to A

  client-A -----attach----> SBA -----forward----> Runtime(s-1)
                 |                        ^
                 |<----stream/resp--------|

Failure modes and heuristics:
- If runtime returns cache-miss spike (P95 latency high), SBA can: 1) spawn temporary dedicated s-session, 2) fall back to a smaller model variant, 3) return graceful degraded response and mark the call for async replay.
- When client disconnects mid-generation: keep the currently executing token stream alive for N seconds (configurable) if there are other attached clients that might reuse the prefix; else cancel.

Billing and provenance:
- Track per-client token accounting at the SBA layer by attributing tokens consumed in response to the active overlay and request metadata.
- Include a provenance header on runtime calls: X-Bridge-Provenance: c_session=c-xxx; overlay_id=ov-12; attach_point=s-1

KV snapshot format (sketch, textual):
- header: {"version":"1", "s_session":"s-yyy", "created_at":"..."}
- body: base_prompt: string
        kv_keys: ["k1","k2"], (values stored separately or compressed)
        anchors: [{"label":"last_high_level","offset":123}]
- rationale: keep snapshots small (<16KB) for quick resume over mobile networks

Example minimal attach+call (HTTP/1.1 single request path):
POST /v1/sba/calls
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <c-resume-token>
Body: {
  "c_session_id":"c-7b3",
  "input": {"text":"Write a one-line summary of my last message"},
  "attach_hint": {"prefetch": true} 
}
Response: stream chunks: {"event":"token","text":"..."}
Final: {"meta":{"tokens":42,"provenance":"X-Bridge-Provenance:..."}}

Design questions / TODOs (big list):
- How to enforce strict isolation for regulated tenants while still enabling sharing? Option: tiered s_sessions where some are encrypted-per-tenant (HSM-bound) and cannot share KV.
- Garbage collection of overlays: LRU? TTL? client-initiated snapshot + release?
- Can we reuse existing Redwood model-rollout fallback logic, or does SBA need custom fallback orchestration?
- Metrics: per-s_session cache hit rate, per-c_session latency tail, overlay memory usage, snapshot size distribution.
- Security: ensure resume tokens are windowed and rotate to avoid stolen-token abuse. Tie resume tokens to device fingerprints? (privacy tradeoffs)

Interoperability notes with Redwood runtime:
- The runtime should expose a "inject_overlay(prefix_id, overlay_ops)" micro-op to apply overlays cheaply without duplicating KV cache entries.
- runtime must accept provenance headers so logs and evictions can attribute correctly.

Open experiments to run:
- Synthetic workload: 1000 c_sessions -> 1 s_session, with 10–20% prefix overlap. Measure P95 latency and token cost.
- Prefetch policy: on attach, look at last N client messages and warm top-3 KV keys predicted by heuristic.

Quick mental performance estimates:
- If overlay application cost is O(n_ops) where n_ops ~ 10, overhead per request should be <5ms in SBA hot path (target).
- Network savings for shared prefixes: potentially 30–60% token reduction for chatty clients that repeat system instruction.

Short-term next steps (for myself):
- sketch a minimal prototype: a lightweight python service that implements attach/call and uses Redwood hosted API as backend (no runtime changes) to validate savings.
- draft a short RFC for eng-serving-runtime outlining required micro-ops + provenance headers.
- add basic metrics to prototype: per-call cache-hits and delta-size.

Notes to self / random thoughts:
- Might want to call the snapshot format "bridge-checkpoint" not snapshot — clearer semantics for resume.
- Consider hooking SBA into Optimize to suggest best s_session_mode per-tenant.
- Keep device-local small snapshot so users can resume offline (encrypted with device key) — need to think through key management.

References and inspiration:
- saw similar patterns in internal notes on prefix caching (ENG-2190) and mobile-offline heuristics.
- related: conversation-handoff patterns (existing doc), but this is intentionally more runtime-focused.

Unresolved edge-cases:
- If two clients simultaneously write contradictory edits to a shared overlay (rare), how to reconcile? For now: deterministic merge based on sequence id; if conflict, last-writer wins and mark delta.
- When to evict anchor keys from shared KV when memory pressure? Maybe LRU with tenant-safe threshold.

If you read this later: treat as exploratory. Will extract an RFC once we have prototype numbers.

--- end of scratchbook ---
